rationale: Fires on a SYN to tcp.dest_port 22, the SYN-ACK and 2 more SYNs from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst (3 s between events, 5 s in all): it counts connections, not failed logins, so 3 successive logins or ssh/scp automation also fire (false-positive-prone, #40).

Fires when an ARP request (arp.ar_op == 1) is answered by 2 replies for the requested address (arp.ar_sip == arp.ar_tip.1) with different arp.ar_sha within 4 s: the RFC 5227 address-conflict signature of ARP spoofing, also produced by a misconfigured or failing-over device.

Fires on 2 ARP replies (arp.ar_op == 2) for the same arp.ar_sip with a different arp.ar_sha within 4 s: one address claimed by 2 MAC addresses, which ARP cache poisoning produces, but so do a duplicate address or a failover.

Fires on a SYN followed by a reverse ACK whose tcp.ack_nb differs from the SYN's tcp.seq_nb by 791101 (0xC123D), the magic sequence delta of the SYNful Knock router implant, which ATT&CK lists under Traffic Signaling (the draft's T1046 fits only a scanner looking for implants).

Fires when 2 consecutive fragments of the same ip.src/ip.dst flow carry a different ip.opts_type: inconsistent IP options across fragments is a malformed-packet or IDS-evasion trait on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on an IP fragment (ip.mf_flag > 0) with ip.tot_len < 28, or < 40 at ip.frag_offset 0: an undersized fragment is malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on any frame with meta.packet_len < 34: a too-short packet is malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a SYN (tcp.flags == 2) with tcp.payload_len > 0: data in a SYN is allowed (TCP Fast Open) and odd on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on an HTTP request whose http.user_agent contains 'Nikto', the default User-Agent of the Nikto web vulnerability scanner.
Fires on any GRE packet with gre.version > 0: an invalid GRE version is malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.

Fires on 4 ICMP redirects (icmp.type == 5) between the same ip.src and ip.dst, 3 s apart at most: 4 packets are too few for the draft's network flood (T1498.001), while forged redirects reroute a victim's traffic through the sender, an adversary-in-the-middle move that ATT&CK has no sub-technique for.
Fires on 2 fragments of the same ip.identification that both have ip.frag_offset == 0: allowed but odd fragmentation (possible IDS evasion) on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires when a later fragment of the same ip.identification starts less than 9 offset units after the previous one: tiny fragments are an IDS-evasion trait on their own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Same as rule 22 for out-of-order fragments (ip.frag_offset < ip.frag_offset.1 and a difference < 9): an IDS-evasion trait on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires when 2 fragments of the same ip.identification overlap (offset difference < ip.tot_len): overlapping fragments are an IDS-evasion trait on their own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Same as rule 24 for out-of-order overlapping fragments: an IDS-evasion trait on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.

Fires on 4 packets from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst with 4 different ip.proto_id values, 10 ms apart at most: an IP protocol scan (nmap -sO), which probes which protocols the host answers rather than which ports.

Fires on 4 UDP packets (ip.proto_id == 17) from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst with 4 different udp.dest_port, 10 ms apart at most: a UDP port scan pattern, but ordinary client traffic also produces it and it is known to fire on normal traffic (false-positive-prone).
Fires on a TCP packet with tcp.urg, tcp.fin and tcp.psh all set: the Xmas-scan probe, a flag combination with no legitimate use.

Fires when ip.src or ip.dst is in the rule's built-in list of botnet command-and-control addresses (em_check_botnetcc), whatever the protocol, so only the parent technique applies; the list is static and ages.
Fires on an HTTP GET whose http.uri is in the rule's built-in list of trojan check-in URIs (em_check_trojan_uri): malware C2 over HTTP, as long as the static list stays current.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application or System Exploitation
rationale: Fires on a single HTTP GET whose http.user_agent is longer than 256 characters: one oversized header is an attempt to crash the parser rather than the draft's flood (T1499.002), and some legitimate clients send long User-Agent strings.

Fires when http.host is one of 5 hard-coded WannaCry kill-switch domains (em_check_WannaCry): an infected host's HTTP check of its kill switch, not the SMB exploit (EternalBlue) that the draft's T1210 describes, and ATT&CK has no technique for a kill-switch check.
Fires when ip.src or ip.dst is in the rule's built-in list of Tor node addresses (em_check_tor_ip): Tor use, which is not malicious on its own, and the static relay list ages.
Fires on 4 SYNs (tcp.flags == 2) from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst on 4 different tcp.dest_port, 10 ms apart at most: a TCP SYN/connect port scan.
Fires on 4 SCTP INIT chunks (sctp.ch_type == 1) from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst on 4 different sctp.dest_port, 10 ms apart at most: an SCTP INIT port scan.
Fires on 4 TCP packets with no flag (tcp.flags == 0) from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst on 4 different tcp.dest_port, 10 ms apart at most: a TCP NULL scan.
Fires on 4 bare FIN packets (tcp.flags == 1) from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst on 4 different tcp.dest_port, 10 ms apart at most: a TCP FIN scan.

Fires on 4 bare ACK packets (tcp.flags == 16) from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst on 4 different tcp.dest_port, 10 ms apart at most: a TCP ACK/Window scan, though a client with several open connections to one host can send the same.

Fires on 4 FIN/ACK packets (tcp.flags == 17) from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst on 4 different tcp.dest_port, 10 ms apart at most: a TCP Maimon scan, though closing several connections to one host at once sends the same.
Fires on 4 SCTP COOKIE ECHO chunks (sctp.ch_type == 10) from the same ip.src to the same ip.dst on 4 different sctp.dest_port, 10 ms apart at most: an SCTP COOKIE ECHO port scan.

Fires on a TCP RST (tcp.rst == 1) then 3 SYNs from the same ip.src and tcp.src_port to the same ip.dst on different ports: a port scan, but nothing checks the zombie (third host or IP ID probing), so a plain nmap -sS also fires (false-positive-prone for 'idle scan', #40).

Fires on 4 FTP PORT commands with 4 different ftp.packet_request_parameter from the same client to the same server within 3 s each: it never compares the PORT address with the client's ip.src, the mark of a bounce, so an active-mode client fetching 4 files fires (false-positive-prone, #40).

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application or System Exploitation
rationale: Fires on a reassembled ICMP packet ((ip.df_flag + ip.mf_flag) == 0) with meta.packet_len > 65535: the ping of death, an oversized datagram that crashes vulnerable IP stacks.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application or System Exploitation
rationale: Fires when a fragment with ip.mf_flag == 1 follows the last fragment of the same ip.identification (100 ms between the first 2 events, 150 ms in all): the Nestea malformed-fragment pattern, which crashes vulnerable IP stacks.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application or System Exploitation
rationale: Fires on a reassembled IP packet ((ip.df_flag + ip.mf_flag) == 0) with meta.packet_len > 65535, any protocol: a fragment overrun, used to crash vulnerable IP stacks.

Fires when tcp.p_payload contains the EICAR antivirus test string (em_check_eicar_virus): EICAR is harmless and stands in for malware transferred over the network, and the direction of the transfer is not checked.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: OS Exhaustion Flood
rationale: Fires on a SYN followed by 3 SYN-ACKs back to its sender (50 ms between events, 100 ms in all); no RST or missing final ACK is checked, so a client opening 3 connections to a server fires, and it is known to fire on normal traffic (false-positive-prone).
Fires on any packet whose ip.version is neither 4 nor 6: a bogus IP version is malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on an IP packet whose ip.opts_type is not a standard IP option number (em_check_ip_opt): malformed or experimental traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on an IP packet whose ip.proto_id is unassigned or reserved (em_check_ip_proto_id): odd traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on an IP packet with non-zero padding (ip.padding_check != 0): malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on an IP packet with the reserved flag set (ip.rf_flag != 0): malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on any TCP packet with tcp.urg != 0: the urgent flag is allowed and only odd on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires when the reassembled upstream TCP session payload (tcp.tcp_session_payload_up) contains the EICAR test string: a stand-in for malware transferred over the network, direction not checked.

Fires when tcp.p_payload contains the full EICAR test string (em_check_eicar_virus_http, which checks no HTTP field despite its name): a stand-in for malware transferred over the network, direction not checked.

Meant to catch 2 Content-Encoding headers, but em_check_double_compression_http returns true as soon as tcp.p_payload contains one 'Content-Encoding', so every compressed HTTP message fires (false-positive-prone); a double encoding hides a payload from inspection, a judgement call between exploit and evasion.

Meant to catch 2 Transfer-Encoding headers, or Transfer-Encoding with Content-length (HTTP request smuggling), but em_check_double_encoding_http returns true as soon as tcp.p_payload contains one 'Transfer-Encoding', so every chunked HTTP message fires (false-positive-prone).
Fires when tcp.p_payload contains the version token 'HTTP/1.01 ' (em_check_version_http): an odd HTTP version on its own, with no exploit behind it, so not the draft's T1190.
Same as rule 54 over IPv6 (ipv6.src != ipv6.dst): the EICAR test string in tcp.p_payload, a stand-in for malware transferred over the network.

Fires when the protocol hierarchy of a packet is longer than 14 layers (em_check_max_proto_len): deep encapsulation is odd on its own and can come from legitimate tunnels, with no specific ATT&CK technique.
Fires when 2 fragments of the same ip.identification have a different ip.proto_ttl: non-homogeneous TTL is an IDS-evasion trait on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.

Fires when tcp.p_payload contains 'Transfer-Encoding::chunked' (em_check_header_http): an obfuscated framing header used for request smuggling or to slip past inspection, a judgement call between exploit and evasion.

Fires when the URL-decoded, lower-cased http.uri or http.user_agent contains one of the obfuscated ${jndi:ldap://} or ${jndi:rmi://} lookup strings of em_check_log4shell (14 of 16 can match; a plain ${jndi:ldap:// is not in the list): the Log4Shell JNDI lookup injection; the rule's description cites CVE-2021-44832, a different Log4j flaw (JDBC Appender configuration).
Type TEST: fires on In-band Network Telemetry (int.packet_count > 0) with int.hop_switch_ids set, a validity check of INT, not an attack.
Type SECURITY: fires on DTLS whose dtls.version or client-hello cipher suites are not in the allow list (MMT_SEC_DTLS_CIPHER_ALLOWLIST), a configuration-compliance check, not an attack technique.

Fires on 2 NAS Security Mode Complete messages (nas_5g.security_type == 4) of the same ngap.amf_ue_id with the same NAS sequence number and MAC but different payload: a 5G NAS replay, which ATT&CK Enterprise does not cover (MITRE FiGHT does).

Fires when an Authentication Response (nas_5g.message_type == 87) on the same SCTP stream and ngap.amf_ue_id as the Authentication Request carries a different ngap.ran_ue_id: a 5G UE authentication hijack, which ATT&CK Enterprise does not cover.
Fires on SCTP to port 38412 (NGAP) whose sctp_data.data_ppid is neither 60 (NGAP) nor 46: a wrong payload protocol identifier is malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on SCTP to port 38412 with sctp_data.data_ppid == 60 whose payload does not decode as NGAP (no ngap.procedure_code): malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
rationale: Fires on 2 NGAP InitialUEMessage (ngap.procedure_code == 15) with the same ngap.ran_ue_id within 0.1 ms: a signalling-storm marker against the AMF, but 2 messages are a thin basis for a flood.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
rationale: Fires when the count of NGAP InitialUEMessage (ngap.procedure_code == 15, port 38412) in the current millisecond reaches MMT_SEC_5G_DOS_NGAP_INITIALUEMESSAGE_MS_LIMIT, a control-plane flood against the AMF; when the variable is unset the limit is 0 and every InitialUEMessage fires (false-positive-prone by default).

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
rationale: Fires when the count of HTTP/2 GET or POST headers (http2.header_method 130 or 131) or WINDOW_UPDATE frames (http2.type == 8) in the current millisecond reaches MMT_SEC_5G_DOS_HTTP2_MS_LIMIT (80 when unset): an HTTP/2 flood against a 5G core service.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application or System Exploitation
rationale: Fires on an HTTP/2 POST (http2.header_method == 131) whose http2.header_length is between 351 and 16383: a large header block, the shape of an HPACK compression bomb (a DoS, not the draft's T1190), but ordinary POSTs with large cookies or tokens fire too.

Fires on an HTTP/2 POST whose payload contains a backslash, '#', '%' or '$' after its 9th byte (em_check_fuzzing): meant to spot fuzzing, but any URL-encoded or JSON body can contain these characters (false-positive-prone).
Fires on a DICOM PDU with dicom.pdu_type > 7: an invalid PDU type is malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF (dicom.pdu_type == 4) whose dicom.command_field is none of the standard DIMSE command values: malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF whose dicom.status is neither 0 (success) nor 0xFF00 (pending): warnings and errors are normal protocol outcomes, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF with dicom.status == 0xDEAD, a value no standard status uses: a fuzzing artefact on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF with dicom.message_id == 0: an odd value on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF with dicom.message_id == 0xFFFF: a boundary value on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF whose dicom.data_set_type is neither 0x0001 nor 0x0101: malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on DICOM traffic with dicom.pdu_len > 16777216 (16 MB): an oversized length field is malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM PDU with dicom.pdu_len == 0: malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ or -AC (dicom.pdu_type 1 or 2) whose dicom.proto_version is not 1: malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF with dicom.pdv_length < 4: malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF with dicom.pdv_flags > 3: malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on any DICOM C-CANCEL (dicom.command_field == 0x0FFF): a legitimate command, odd only out of context, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM command whose dicom.command_field has the response bit set (>= 0x8000): it does not check the direction, so normal responses also match; a protocol anomaly with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on every DICOM A-ABORT (dicom.pdu_type == 7), a legitimate PDU: a protocol event, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF with dicom.pdv_context == 0, an invalid presentation context ID: a state-machine anomaly, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ (dicom.pdu_type == 1) seen within 5 s after a P-DATA-TF (dicom.pdu_type == 4), with no flow constraint: a protocol-sequence anomaly, with no ATT&CK technique.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Application or System Exploitation
rationale: Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ/AC whose dicom.application_context contains a format specifier (%s, %x, %n, %p, %d, %0, %., %-): the CVE-2024-23914 format string in Merge DICOM Toolkit's MC_Open_Association(), which crashes the requesting side (availability impact only), so a DoS rather than the draft's T1190.

Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF whose dicom.affected_sop_class_uid contains a traversal pattern (../, ..\, ..%2f, /etc/, \windows\): the DCMTK path traversal the rule cites (CVE-2022-2119 server side, CVE-2022-2120 client side), but the records do not name the field, and DCMTK may build file names from another UID than the one checked here.

Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ whose dicom.called_ae_title is longer than 16 characters, an overflow attempt on the 16-byte AE Title; the rule cites CVE-2015-8979, but that record is an overflow in parsePresentationContext, not in the AE Title, so no CVE is attached.

technique_name: Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
rationale: Meant to fire on more than 20 DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ in 5 s, but em_check_assoc_flood reads meta.utime (a struct timeval) as microseconds, so its window never resets in practice and every A-ASSOCIATE-RQ from any source fires once 20 have been seen since start (false-positive-prone).

Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ whose dicom.called_ae_title contains a keyword such as ATTACKER, EVIL or ROGUE, or a character other than a letter, digit, space or underscore: a lab-test marker that legal AE titles with '-' or '.' also match, with no ATT&CK technique.

Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF whose dicom.patient_name contains an injection pattern (' OR, 1=1, -- , <script, alert(, ../, %s, %n, ${jndi) (em_check_patient_injection): an injection attempt against the PACS or the applications that display the name.

Fires once 5 DICOM P-DATA-TF with '*' or '?' in dicom.patient_name have been seen since start (em_check_wildcard_enum, a counter that never resets): bulk enumeration of patient records, but wildcard C-FIND is also normal PACS use.
Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ/AC with dicom.pdu_len < 68, below the minimum size: malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ whose dicom.abstract_syntax is not an OID (em_check_invalid_syntax): malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM A-RELEASE-RQ/RP or A-ABORT (dicom.pdu_type 5 to 7) whose dicom.pdu_len is not 4: malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ/AC with dicom.pdu_len > 4096: unusual but legal size, with no ATT&CK technique.

Fires on a DICOM A-ASSOCIATE-RQ whose called and calling AE titles are the swap of the first association seen since start (em_check_ae_swap): a role reversal that a C-MOVE redirection may cause, with no clear ATT&CK technique.
Fires on a DICOM P-DATA-TF where dicom.pdv_length + 4 differs from dicom.pdu_len (em_check_pdv_pdu_mismatch): a length inconsistency, malformed traffic on its own, with no ATT&CK technique.
